definition: Evanescent means lasting only a moment before vanishing.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word evanescent. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know evanescent should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: An evanescent hush fell over the stadium between the kick and the roar, gone before anyone could name it.
Temporary is far milder than evanescent — it promises only that a thing ends someday, maybe years out, while an evanescent hush is dissolving in the same breath that announces it.
Short-lived stops short of evanescent: a short-lived fashion still gets its season, while an evanescent glow is dissolving in the very moment you notice it.

Vanishing reports a disappearance in progress — the ship is vanishing into the fog right now, whatever the ship is normally like. Evanescent makes the fading a built-in character: an evanescent glow was always going to dissolve almost as it formed. Vanishing describes an event; evanescent describes a nature.

Fleeting is about speed — a fleeting glance, a fleeting thought, here and gone almost at once. A fleeting moment simply ends fast. Evanescent adds a picture: the thing visibly dissolves as it appears, mist thinning while you watch, the fade itself on display before your eyes.

Its neighbor in this unit, transient, is the cooler word: a transient guest still unpacks a bag and stays a while.
Say transient for people, populations, and symptoms; save evanescent for what is fading even as you point at it.
